question: Does the root-mediated Docker, iptables, and attestation design provide an acceptable long-term security boundary for running untrusted Mantis candidate code?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes the trust model and privileged execution surface; that acceptance decision cannot be inferred from focused tests or static checks alone.

options.title: Approve the isolation boundary after audit
options.body: Accept this design after a security-focused review of the exact workflow, wrapper, mounts, input validation, network rules, and cleanup semantics.

options.title: Narrow the trusted runner
options.body: Require a smaller or less-privileged execution design before accepting the candidate-proof workflow.

options.title: Pause the proof lane
options.body: Keep the existing safe failure behavior until a maintainer-approved isolation design is available.

recommendation.title: Approve the isolation boundary after audit
recommendation.body: Accept this design after a security-focused review of the exact workflow, wrapper, mounts, input validation, network rules, and cleanup semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged and current work places this contributor closest to the Mantis proof-harness design, while final acceptance should come from the repository’s security or workflow owners.
